# Congressional trade disclosures: is there an edge? (Research Inc., 2026-10-07)

**Verdict: No usable edge from the disclosure date after costs for a long-only swing desk on our 20 tickers. No signals.json changes.**

## 1. Evidence
- **Pre-STOCK Act, positive but measured from the trade date:** Senate purchases beat the market by 85 bp/month from 1993 to 1998 ([Ziobrowski, JFQA 2004](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-financial-and-quantitative-analysis/article/abnormal-returns-from-the-common-stock-investments-of-the-us-senate/A39406479940758D59E09FDCB8EE9BEC)). House purchases beat it by 55 bp/month from 1985 to 2001 ([2011](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/business-and-politics/article/abnormal-returns-from-the-common-stock-investments-of-members-of-the-us-house-of-representatives/BC6C6A524BBE96738BB94D37EF0FD1A5)).
- **Rebuttal:** actual portfolios lagged the market by 2 to 3% a year from 2004 to 2008 ([Eggers & Hainmueller, JOP 2013](https://andy.egge.rs/papers/EggMueller_capitol_losses_jop_2013.pdf)).
- **Post-STOCK Act, null:** in 2012 to 2020, stocks House members bought lagged by 26 bp over 6 months, consistent with random picking ([Belmont et al., J. Public Econ 2022](https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/pubeco/v207y2022ics0047272722000044.html)). For 2012 to 2023, Congress "underperform[s] or, at best, match[es]" benchmarks, and its trades follow analyst calls and retail sentiment ([Chen & Sacerdote, NBER w35041, 2026](https://www.nber.org/papers/w35041)).
- **Disclosure date:** a House purchase disclosure adds about 17 to 29 bp on the day it posts ([working paper, 2014–22](https://www.nancyxu.net/_files/ugd/efd0b7_87e658565baa4d99b039f7f2aa87979e.pdf)). For the typical trade the effect is about zero, with larger trades popping more near 2024 as copy-trading grew ([Houghton/Penn 2026](https://exa.ai/library/publication/xd55hvfq47n)). That's a one-day pop, not a multi-week drift.

## 2. ETFs (free Yahoo chart feed, adjusted closes with dividends, through the Oct 6, 2026 close)
| | Since 2/7/2023 launch | YTD | 1 yr | Expense ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| NANC (Dem) | +112.8% (22.9%/yr) | +17.2% | +19.5% | 0.72% |
| GOP, formerly KRUZ (Rep) | +85.5% (18.4%/yr) | +25.7% | +25.8% | 0.73% |
| SPY | +96.7% (20.3%/yr) | +15.1% | +17.7% | — |
| QQQ | +150.4% | +24.1% | — | — |

- KRUZ became GOP on 3/21/2025 ([SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1742912/000199937125002790/kruz-497_031825.htm)). Unusual Whales [exited both funds](https://unusualwhales.substack.com/p/important-unusual-whales-no-longer) in Aug 2026.
- NANC has a beta of 1.13 and its top weights are NVDA, MSFT, and GOOG ([stockanalysis](https://stockanalysis.com/etf/nanc/)). Its 2.6 pts a year over SPY is a tech tilt, and it trailed QQQ badly. stockanalysis shows a wrong 2019 inception date. GOP trails SPY since launch. The GOP expense ratio is from [Schwab](https://www.schwab.wallst.com/Prospect/Research/etfs/summary.asp?symbol=gop).
- **Rebalancing:** the funds are active. They trade as PTRs post, weight by the midpoints of the reported dollar ranges, and **exclude options trades** ([prospectus](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1742912/000199937126001899/nanc-497k_012826.htm)), so they don't copy Pelosi's options.

## 3. Data sources
- **Free with no signup:** the [House Clerk bulk index](https://disclosures-clerk.house.gov/public_disc/financial-pdfs/2026FD.zip) is updated daily as XML and lists PTR type "P", filing date, and DocID. Each PTR is a PDF at `ptr-pdfs/2026/{DocID}.pdf` and parses with pdftotext. I tested both.
- **Senate [eFD](https://efdsearch.senate.gov/):** free, but it requires accepting terms and serves HTML and scanned PDFs.
- **Flagged, not used:** the Quiver API returns 401 (key or paid plan). The House/Senate Stock Watcher S3 feeds return 403 (dead). Capitol Trades and Unusual Whales are free to browse but have no free documented API, and the Unusual Whales API is paid.
- **Legal:** EIGA bars using PTRs for "commercial purpose," a [risk the funds disclose](https://subversiveetfs.com/). Paper trading is non-commercial.

## 4. Why no edge for us
- **Lag:** filings can come 45 days late. Pelosi's Dec 24 trades were filed Jan 23.
- **Pelosi in 2026:** only 4 PTRs. January paired GOOGL/AMZN/AAPL/NVDA call buys with $1 to $25M partial stock sales of the same names, which is a mixed signal. Her later filings were INTC, UBER, BE, and real estate, all off our list.
- **Crowding:** any pop happens on disclosure day, before a swing entry.
- **Cherry-picking:** viral claims track one survivor during a tech bull run, which is QQQ beta.

## 5. signals.json
**No integration.** It would add noise correlated with QQQ that our relative-strength rotation already captures. The only cheap use is a one-line context note in a brief when a disclosure of $1M or more hits a listed ticker. It wouldn't be an engine input or a tiebreaker. If Tendies and Dip wants to falsify this anyway, here's a test spec using the House index: buy at the next open after the filing date, hold 10 trading days, compare with SPY, and charge 10 bp round-trip.
